title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Withdrawal Fees an Account Bears for a Cycle
content:
Part of a replenishing automatic transfer for a Savings & Money Market Accounts product is the withdrawal charge the account is left carrying for the statement cycle concerned. This page defines that figure, called here the fee burden, and the state of the ledger it has to be read from.

## Definition

The fee burden for the cycle is the combined amount of the excess withdrawal fee entries that belong to the cycle, less the combined amount of each refund of an excess withdrawal fee that posted in the cycle. A refund on either ground, bank error or courtesy, lowers the burden. A negative figure is treated as zero.

## What the figure must reflect

The fee burden describes what the account carries for the cycle as the charter settles it. It is read from a cycle record on which each excess withdrawal fee the charter makes due for the cycle stands charged, and each refund of such a fee that the account is entitled to stands credited. A total read from a record that lacks a fee the charter makes due, or lacks a refund the account is entitled to, is not the figure this policy defines.

The ledger is fit to be read only when both of these hold, each of them borne out by the records and neither of them checked by the amount itself:

- no entry on the account carries a posting date later than the current date; a charge or refund made at a weekend or on a Federal Reserve holiday posts on the next business day, so a later-dated entry shows the record is still unsettled;
- any excess withdrawal fee refund dated within the cycle returns a fee that itself belongs to that cycle, as the source item named on the refund shows.

If either fails, no amount is worked out under this policy.

## Worked example (hypothetical cycle)

| Entry | Amount |
|---|---|
| Excess withdrawal fee | 12.50 |
| Excess withdrawal fee | 12.50 |
| Excess withdrawal fee | 12.50 |
| Refund of one of those charges, courtesy | 12.50 |

Fee burden: 37.50 less 12.50, which is 25.00.

## Points of judgement

**Does a courtesy refund lower the burden, although the fee was properly charged?** Yes. Whatever its ground, a refund of an excess withdrawal fee that posted during the cycle lowers it.
